relations.evidence: raṃganātha tanūjaneḥ(!) || daivajña vālakṛṣṇasya sūnunā bhānu śarmaṇā

date.as_written: nabho gajadhṛti miteśake vikrama bhūpateḥ || māghe māsi site pakṣe pakṣatyāṃ ravi vāsare

notes: The chronogram nabhas (0), gaja (8), dhṛti (18), read right to left, gives 1880. 'śake vikrama bhūpateḥ' names the era of King Vikrama, so this is VS 1880, not ŚS 1880 as the catalogue says. 'śaka' here just means 'era'. VS 1880 corresponds to 1823/24 CE. Māgha śukla pratipad of that year falls in Jan/Feb 1824 CE. The colophon breaks off after the date ('------- ///'), so the verb that would make Bhānuśarman the scribe is lost. Even so, the verse with the instrumental 'bhānu śarmaṇā' almost certainly names the copyist. 'vidvajjanasabhādhīra' is an epithet of Raṅganātha, not a title. 'khakhākaiḥ ślokai' (= 900 ślokas, read right to left) is the extent of the text, not a date. 'tanūjaneḥ(!)' is a mistake for 'tanūjanuṣaḥ'/'tanūjasya' ('son of'), and agrees with 'vālakṛṣṇasya'.
